# 1 Clement Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 36

**36:1** This, dear friends, is the way in which we found our salvation: Jesus Christ — the high priest of our offerings, the guardian and defender of our weakness.

**36:2** Through him we lift our eyes to the heights of heaven. Through him we behold his faultless and most exalted face as in a mirror. Through him the eyes of our hearts have been opened. Through him our foolish and darkened minds have come to life in the wonderful light of his knowledge. Through him the Lord has willed that we taste immortal knowledge — he who is "the radiance of his glory and the express image of his being, sustaining all things by the word of his power" — at whose right hand angels, archangels, powers, thrones, and dominions stand arrayed, offering worship.

**36:3** Before him, in the splendor and excellence of his beauty, stand the six-winged and many-eyed ones — the seraphim and the cherubim — crying out: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole creation is full of his glory."

**36:4** And so let us too, gathered together as one, cry out to him eagerly as with a single voice, that we may share in his great and glorious promises.

**36:5** For scripture says: "No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined the things he has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*PNEUMA renders the anaphoric "through him" (v. 2) sequence with maximum rhetorical impact. "Express image" (v. 2) echoes the KJV of Hebrews 1:3 (*charakter*), preserving a well-known English christological phrase.*
